title: Sporadic cold-start cascade from backfill + burst-replenish race causing reserved-pool depletion
creator: Maya Chen
description: Several customers experienced simultaneous 5xx errors and sustained latency spikes during an overnight maintenance window. Root cause appears to be an interaction between the backfill service (which replenishes tenant burst credits) and the autoscaler’s warmup preheat logic: many tenants were scheduled to replenish at the same time, triggering simultaneous warmup tasks that caused allocator saturation, rapid reserved-pool headroom consumption, and then emergency shedding. This ticket tracks the incident, immediate mitigations applied, the short-term patch, and longer-term resilience work.
symptoms:
- 503 errors and request timeouts for 18 minutes across multiple tenants in EU-west-1 and us-east-1
- Token-level latency up to 3x baseline during warmup cascade
- Reserved pool headroom dropped to 6% triggering burst gating and customer-facing denials
- Console alerts: burst_replenish_rate spike, allocator_queue_length spike, pool_headroom low
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create 200 small tenants with burst credits nearly depleted.
2) Schedule backfill service to top up credits at the same timestamp (simulate a cron alignment).
3) Observe allocator warmup tasks spawn concurrently; monitor reserved-pool headroom and allocator queue.
4) If allocator saturates, API starts returning 503s after headroom threshold crossed.
Note: we reproduced locally by simulating warmup handlers and a mocked allocator service under a 4 GPU reserved pool.
impact_details: Affected ~12 enterprise tenants (billing tier: Dedicated) during high overnight throughput. Customer-reported incidents from two accounts (AcmeHealth, AtlasForms). Estimated revenue risk for window: medium-high. SLA alerts triggered for latency and error-rate. Engineering pager fired twice.
immediate_mitigation:
- Throttled backfill service to add jitter and a randomized stagger window (+30s-5m)
- Enabled emergency headroom holdback: reserve 20% of reserved pool capacity for safety during replenishment windows
- Routed critical VIP tenants to hosted fallback model in different AZ for 40 minutes
- Opened support threads with affected customers with status updates
short_term_fix: Apply a patch to backfill controller to implement exponential backoff + coordinated jitter and a concurrency cap per AZ. Modify allocator admission to honor a per-tenant warmup token bucket so warmups are rate-limited. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/1125
long_term_plan:
1) Redesign backfill scheduling: use distributed lease + stagger policy and add tenant-priority decay.
2) Extend autoscaler to include warmup orchestration with fairness (fairshare warmup queue), preheat pacing, and per-tenant burst throttles.
3) Add predictive headroom predictor that simulates bulk replenishment events.
4) Run canary in eu-west-1 for 72 hours before global rollout.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge short-term patches to release branch autoscaler-2.8.1 (hotfix).
2) Canary deploy to non-production then to EU-west-1 dedicated pools with feature flag backfill_jitter=true.
3) Monitor pool_headroom, allocator_queue_length, and customer 5xx; if stable 72h, enable globally.
4) Schedule long-term refactor in Q2 cycle with product sign-off.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- New alert: backfill_concurrent_warmups > 30 for 5m
- Dashboard: reserved_pool_headroom by AZ + tenant-category
- SLO check: 99th percentile token latency for warmup window
- Post-deploy: synthetic traffic test that simulates staggered replenishment

postmortem_notes: Preliminary: the system assumed independent replenishment events. A scheduler edge-case aligned many tenant replenishments to identical cron boundaries across regions. Weaknesses: backfill had no global coordination, warmup tasks did not participate in autoscaler fairness model, and reserved-pool headroom accounting did not consider in-flight warmups. Next steps: full postmortem doc with timeline and RCA due by 2026-03-21.
